title: GPU-resident pre-tokenized data with on-GPU shift augmentation
description: Baseline does 10 steps/s for a 3.2M model at bs 256, i.e. ~100 ms/step where the GPU needs ~5 ms: the Python per-batch tokenizing/padding/shift in the fork's batch() is the bottleneck. Pre-pad everything into one LongTensor on the GPU once and do the abs-shift augmentation as a vectorised op, so a step is an index + a few tensor ops.
hypothesis: 5-8x more steps in the same 240 s (20-30 epochs instead of 4). More training gave run0 held-out greedy 0.99 vs 0.93 here, and a better-converged Stage-1 model should find more proofs in the first EI round, which compounds. Risk: overfitting the cap-6 distribution could hurt transfer beyond 6; the baseline's under-training might be why it beat run0.
surprise: Throughput did NOT change (10 steps/s both), so the Python batching was not the bottleneck and this run is the baseline config with a different RNG stream: 56 -> 67 is a direct measurement of run-to-run noise (~+-10). Kept because the code is simpler on the hot path and GPU-resident data unlocks compile.
